name: userassist_bam_shimcache
description: UserAssist (NTUSER.DAT), BAM and DAM (SYSTEM) and ShimCache / AppCompatCache (SYSTEM) read into records, each with its raw bytes (raw_hex, raw_length) beside what was decoded, the layout and the basis for choosing it, and `unsupported` (with the bytes kept and nothing decoded) when the layout is unknown. source is auto (every source the hive holds), userassist, bam (with dam) or shimcache. UserAssist: Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\UserAssist\{GUID}\Count; the value name is ROT13 (name_raw and name_decoded, ASCII letters only); 72-byte values give session id, run count, focus count, focus time in ms and the last-run FILETIME, 16-byte values give session id, run count and the last-run FILETIME; any other length or type is unsupported. An NTUSER.DAT does not name its owner: sid is null unless owner_sid was given (then it is the caller's word, said in sid_basis). BAM and DAM: ControlSetNNN\Services\bam (and dam)\State\UserSettings\<SID> and the older ...\UserSettings\<SID>; the SID is the name of the key; a 24-byte value gives the last-run FILETIME; the Version and SequenceNumber values are counted (metadata_values_not_listed), not listed. ShimCache: ControlSetNNN\Control\Session Manager\AppCompatCache, the Windows 7 (32-bit and 64-bit entry shapes), 8.0, 8.1 and 10 and later layouts, chosen from the header and the record tags; the time is the file's last-modified time and is never called an execution time; an entry's data blob is counted (data_length) and not decoded or written out; the XP layout, a header that fits none of these, an entry that does not fit its layout and a record whose data size disagrees with its body are unsupported; a header that declares more entries than fit is a problem. All FILETIMEs are given raw (decimal) and as ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits (a zero FILETIME is null). The offsets are those the published notes give; none has been checked against a real hive by the tool's author, and the layout_basis of each record says so. The decoding is this tool's own: the regipy plugins for these sources are not used. Interpretation limits are in every answer (interpretation_limits): presence of a record is not execution, a ShimCache time is not an execution time, and a user whose hive was not collected is not a user with no entry. Second reader: NOT DONE. No RECmd or RegRipper reader is started and cross_check is always {result: not_run}; nothing in the answer is cross-checked by an independent reader. The hive is read as it is: hive_dirty comes from the base block's sequence numbers and the transaction logs beside the hive are named and not replayed. Every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive (a hive of N bytes holds at most N/76 keys and N/20 values), so an index that repeats one list is read to that bound and said under problems; a list is read once. A value over 524288 bytes is counted (raw_length, raw_not_shown) and its bytes are not written out; the answer is then partial. Problems are a page (the first 40 inline, all in all_problems); the records are a page (limit inline, the whole result as JSON Lines named in all_results, never replaced by a smaller one). The tool stops at its own time limit (84 seconds) and says partial, naming at least how many values and ShimCache entries were not read (the values of the key in hand; the keys not started are counted apart, what they hold and the sources after the stop are not counted, and the answer says so). A list of more than 100,000 items, or too long for half the time left, is read in a random order (the answer says so and is partial) instead of in the order of the text shown, so that no key is put in order past the clock; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file. status is complete only when every value of the sources found was read and decoded: an unsupported record, a problem, a record too large to write out, a time stop, a dirty hive and a blind filter each make it partial, and status_basis says which. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (paths, names, publishers and hashes): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). ORDER: the records of each source are taken in the order of the text shown for each key and value name (withheld names in an order of their own that is new for every run), not the order the hive stores them (alphabetical by raw name) and not the order of a ShimCache's own entries, which is its entry_position: what a listing is ordered by is only what the answer shows. FILTERS: `contains` is looked for in the text the answer prints for the path or the decoded and the raw name (never in what the boundary withheld) and `sid` is compared with the printed SID; a record not matched whose printed text holds a withheld part is counted (contains_blind_records) and makes the answer partial, because the needle may be in what is withheld; the name of a result file never depends on a filter's text. A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Past the judging time (SEAL_BUDGET, 10 seconds for an answer or a row, and never past the seal stop of the tool, which is 3.5 seconds before its time limit because the string being judged at that point is finished first and one string of 256 KiB can take up to 2.3 seconds) the strings the evidence supplied are no longer judged: each is replaced whole by <withheld N bytes: backstop: the judging time ran out>, counted and listed, and the answer is partial, except the names this tool wrote itself (its keys, the names of its result files, the name of the hive, its status basis) and a string of 15 characters or fewer made only of letters, digits, _ and . that does not start like a vendor token and, in a field of a typed kind (a SID, a GUID, a digest), fits the grammar of its type (so not a Slack-shaped token, not the value after a flag such as -pwd, not a prefix and 12 characters). The seal stop ends the judging only, not the tool's own work, which has its own, earlier clock. When any part of a free-text string is withheld, the line breaks, tabs and invisible characters of that string are not kept in the text shown (it is judged without them); a string with nothing withheld is shown exactly as it is. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape, five independent runs, 4,940 per shape; rates, not guarantees; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes: 0 printed whole in 4,940 plants of each shape and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: about 0.1% printed whole (0 whole and 1 piece of 12 characters in 4,940 plants of the block's own harness; 1 of 105 canaries end to end, the same canary in four slots; an earlier measurement found 2 whole and 3 pieces in 4,940), so the rate is small and not zero. The shapes that are not zero, as the range of the five runs over all slots with the worst single slot (76 plants, one plant is 1.3%) beside it: 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 1.3%; up to 3.9% in end-to-end runs); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters 0.0% to 0.3% (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24 9.2% to 10.6% (worst slot 14.5% to 21.1%); a 16-character base32 seed 9.8% to 11.7% (worst slot 15.8% to 21.1%). In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Strings changed (any part withheld) on real evidence: in a real 72 MB SOFTWARE hive (3,000 strings sampled per class) 3.7% of key-name components, 1.0% of value names and 0.9% of REG_SZ data (the names of the Windows component store, WinSxS, are not replaced by the backstop in a name, key or path); in real event logs (175 logs, 64,716 records, up to 4 MB each) the XML of 2.0% of the records is replaced whole by the backstop (5.6% before the shape guard of this round; Security 0.1%, was 6.7%), 1.7% of the data fields are withheld (3.7% before, process ids no longer) and 45 of the 175 runs end partial (84 before). The average hides channels: PowerShell/Operational has the XML of 25.0% of its 1,857 records replaced whole (script blocks carry base64 and long identifiers) and CodeIntegrity/Operational 33.3% of its 1,309 (event 3089, whose Hash is a padded base64 digest). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 69% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. DIRTY HIVE: hive_dirty (the two sequence numbers differ), the log files looked for (transaction_logs_looked_for: the hive's name with .LOG1, .LOG2 and .LOG) and the ones beside the hive (transaction_logs_beside_hive) are reported; the logs are NOT replayed, so every answer from a dirty hive is partial and status_basis names the caveat (what is read is the hive file as it is, and keys and values may differ from the live registry; registry_recover replays the logs on a copy, which this tool then reads). A log that is not among the files the job can read is not found: declare the hive's .LOG1 and .LOG2 as inputs of the job. INLINE VALUES: a value whose data is inside its record (four bytes at most) is read from the record for every registry type. regipy 6.3.0 reads up to 2 GiB of the hive file for such a value and returns that for a type it has no branch for (a device property under a Properties key, REG_LINK, REG_FILETIME, an unknown type), so one such value came back as megabytes of the hive; this tool replaces that read. BIG DATA AND REG_MULTI_SZ: the values of a key are read by this tool from regipy's copy of the hive, with regipy 6.3.0's records, names, types and decoding, and a value of more than 16,344 bytes that is kept in segments (a db record) is checked before its data is put together: one that declares more data than the hive file holds past its base block, whose list holds fewer segments than its size needs, runs past the end of the file or names one segment more than once, or one of whose segments lies past the end of the file, is not read; it is named under problems by its place in the key's value list and its type, and the answer is partial (regipy put together whatever the list named: one 16 KB segment named 160 times was a 2.5 MiB value, and a 548 KB hive declared one of 2 GiB). Every value's data counts against the walk's data budget (four times the hive's size) before it is read. A value that declares more than 16 MiB of data is not read: it is named under problems with the length it declares. The values of a key are handed out one at a time and stop at 64 MiB of data for the key, said under problems. A subkey list keeps each key the first time it names it, and is read no further after 4,096 elements in a row that name keys it already named, or past about 190,000 distinct keys (256 MiB of memory), each said under problems; a subkey list begun after the time limit is read to 16,384 elements and a value list to 4,096, and what is left is said. The hive is opened only when its base block and first bin are what regipy's open reads (the regf signature, a first bin of a positive multiple of 4096 bytes, the root cell the base block names inside the bins, allocated and a key, and the first allocated cell of the first bin that same cell): any other file is a failure that says what was found (regipy read a first bin of free space four bytes at a time, with no clock: a 40 MB hive took 58 s). ShimCache entries left at the time limit are counted from the header of a Windows 7 layout, and as at least one for a record layout, never by decoding the rest. A REG_MULTI_SZ is split by this tool in one pass and gives the strings regipy gives (empty ones left out); the bytes after its last NUL, and a string that is not valid UTF-16 with the rest of the data after it, are not in the answer, as with regipy, and are said under problems with their length (regipy dropped them without a word, and took 50 s on 2 MiB with no NUL). The tool's deadline is read before every value and every 256 subkey elements of a list begun before it: the values or subkeys of a key that were not read in time are said under problems.

hive.description: Path to NTUSER.DAT (UserAssist) or SYSTEM (BAM, DAM, ShimCache)

source.description: auto (default: every source the hive holds), userassist, bam (BAM and DAM) or shimcache

contains.description: Keep records whose printed path or name (decoded or raw) contains this text, case-insensitively; looked for only in the text the answer prints

sid.description: Keep records with this SID (the BAM and DAM key name, or owner_sid); compared with the printed SID

owner_sid.description: The SID of the user the NTUSER.DAT belongs to, when the caller knows it: recorded on the UserAssist records as the caller's word, not checked against the hive

limit.description: Records shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); every record is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
